title: Rama's elucidation of dharma to vali
introduction: Rama explains to dying Vali as to why he gave such a punishment. Rama categorically explains all the question put by Vali in the last chapter from the viewpoint of scriptures that lay down principle for sanaatana dharma, eternal tradition, as well as raaja dharma, king's duty. Vali finally concludes that there is someone superior to him and thus seeks refuge in Rama.
closing: There are three kinds of giving. Grudge giving, duty giving, and thanksgiving. Grudge giving says ' I have to...' Duty giving says " I ought to...' Thanksgiving says " I want to...' The first comes from constraint; the second from a sense of obligation; the third from a full heart. This being the saying by an unknown, Vali gave torture to Sugreeva because he had to, Rama gave punishment to Vali because he ought to, and Sugreeva given himself to Rama, because he wanted to. Rama befriends Sugreeva only to take his help in searching Seetha, because Danu, the demon, after release from his curse advises Rama to do so. The killing of Vali is incidental to that befriending. To take help of Sugreeva, he is to be uplifted from his nasty state, and the abuser of tradition Vali is to be resolved. -dīnasya sugreevasya rakṣanam rāmasya dharmaḥ | rājñā dīna jana rakṣnasya parama dharmatvāt | vastuaḥ tu mukhya dharmānusāreṇa eva vāli hananam | -- dharmākūtam

In ānanda rāmayana, sāra kānḍa another treatise of Ramayana, tells that Rama not only accords salvation to Vali but accords a boon to become a tribal in Krishna's incarnation, and kill Krishna at the end, as retaliation to the present killing.
yadi api tvam durācāro nihato asi raṇe mayā | tathā api bhilla rūpeṇa dvāpara ante anghri mama | bhitvā prabhāse bāṇena pūrva vaireṇa vānara
इति वाल्मीकि रामायणे आदि काव्ये किष्किन्ध काण्डे अष्टदशः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 18th chapter in Kishkindha Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
इति उक्तः प्रश्रितम् वाक्यम् धर्म अर्थ सहितम् हितम् |
परुषम् वालिना रामो निहतेन विचेतसा
verses.iast:
iti uktaḥ praśritam vākyam dharma artha sahitam hitam |
paruṣam vālinā rāmo nihatena vicetasā
verses.translation: Thus, Vali who is hit down by arrow and who is collapsing humbly spoke exacting words that contained probity, meaningfulness, and expedience, to Rama.

verses.devanagari:
तम् निष्प्रभम् इव आदित्यम् मुक्त तोयम् इव अंबुदम् |
उक्त वाक्यम् हरि श्रेष्ठम् उपशांतम् इव अनलम्
धर्म अर्थ गुण संपन्नम् हरि ईश्वरम् अनुत्तमम् |
अधिक्षिप्तः तदा रामः पश्चात् वालिनम् अब्रवीत्
verses.iast:
tam niṣprabham iva ādityam mukta toyam iva ambudam |
ukta vākyam hari śreṣṭham upaśāṃtam iva analam
dharma artha guṇa sampannam hari īśvaram anuttamam |
adhikṣiptaḥ tadā rāmaḥ paścāt vālinam abravīt
verses.translation: Then to him who is rendered like a lusterless sun, fizzling out like a cloud that released its water, and who became like a quenched fire, to such a best monkey and an unexcelled lord of monkeys who has just now imputed Rama with words that are abounding with righteousness and meaningfulness, Rama spoke subsequently.
notes: The words Vali spoke contain righteousness from his viewpoint, when he said 'How did you hit me without confronting me...' and the meaningfulness in the words like 'a quarrel comes when gold and silver are the cause, I should have brought Ravana without bloodshed, I would have brought Maithili and presented before your...' etc. But these words are with the death time wisdom of Vali, and they become parroted saying but cannot be practical with the kind of righteousness followed by Vali.

glosses.meaning: he who is arraigned [find fault with
without, luster, sun, like - to lusterless Vali
righteousness, meaningfulness, attributes, abounding with - in the words of Vali
on who has the words spoken, Vali

verses.devanagari:
धर्मम् अर्थम् च कामम् च समयम् च अपि लौकिकम् |
अविज्ञाय कथम् बाल्यात् माम् इह अद्य विगर्हसे
verses.iast:
dharmam artham ca kāmam ca samayam ca api laukikam |
avijñāya katham bālyāt mām iha adya vigarhase
verses.translation: "Uncaring for probity, prosperity, pleasure deriving, and even for the social conventions, now how do you rebuke me childishly in this matter?

verses.devanagari:
अपृष्ट्वा बुद्धि संपन्नान् वृद्धान् आचार्य संमतान् |
सौम्य वानर चापल्यात् त्वम् माम् वक्तुम् इह इच्छसि
verses.iast:
apṛṣṭvā buddhi sampannān vṛddhān ācārya saṃmatān |
saumya vānara cāpalyāt tvam mām vaktum iha icchasi
verses.translation: "Unconsulted are the doyens of your race that are intellectually well off and agreeable to your mentors about rights and wrongs about your deeds, oh, gentle one, how do you wish to debate with me in this matter with your primate's caprice.

glosses.meaning: without, asking, un, asking - unconsulting [about the deeds you undertook]
in this matter, to talk - to debate

verses.devanagari:
इक्ष्वाकूणाम् इयम् भूमिः स शैल वन कानना |
मृग पक्षि मनुष्याणाम् निग्रह अनुग्रहेषु अपि
verses.iast:
ikṣvākūṇām iyam bhūmiḥ sa śaila vana kānanā |
mṛga pakṣi manuṣyāṇām nigraha anugraheṣu api
verses.translation: "This earth with its mountains, woods, and forests, even along with the authority to condone or condemn the animals, birds, and humans on it belongs to Ikshvaku-s.
notes: Vali's question No. 4] 'I have not done any misdeed either in your country or city...' is answered in this, "when entire earth belongs to us where is the question of a city or a particular country?"

glosses.meaning: of animals, of birds, of humans
[authority] to control, to punish, to condone, even in

verses.devanagari:
ताम् पालयति धर्मात्मा भरतः सत्यवान् ऋजुः |
धर्म काम अर्थ तत्त्वज्ञो निग्रह अनुग्रहे रतः
verses.iast:
tām pālayati dharmātmā bharataḥ satyavān ṛjuḥ |
dharma kāma artha tattvajño nigraha anugrahe rataḥ
verses.translation: "He who is virtue-souled, truth-abiding, plain-speaking, and the knower of the import of probity, pleasures, and prosperity, and the one who is concerned in controlling or condoning his subjects, that Bharata is the ruler of earth.

glosses.meaning: virtue-souled one, one who abides truth
probity, pleasures prosperity, import, knower of
in controlling, in condoning, concerned in

verses.devanagari:
नयः च विनयः च उभौ यस्मिन् सत्यम् च सुस्थितम् |
विक्रमः च यथा दृष्टः स राजा देश कालवित्
verses.iast:
nayaḥ ca vinayaḥ ca ubhau yasmin satyam ca susthitam |
vikramaḥ ca yathā dṛṣṭaḥ sa rājā deśa kālavit
verses.translation: "In whom both scrupulousness and benignancy are there, truthfulness is firmed up, and valour as evinced by scriptures is evident, and he who is the knower of time and place is the king, namely Bharata.

glosses.meaning: scrupulousness, also, benignancy, both are there
valour, also, as has been, seen [stipulated by scriptures]
he is, place, time, knower, king.

verses.devanagari:
तस्य धर्म कृत आदेशा वयम् अन्ये च पार्थिवः |
चरामो वसुधाम् कृत्स्नाम् धर्म संतानम् इच्छवः
verses.iast:
tasya dharma kṛta ādeśā vayam anye ca pārthivaḥ |
carāmo vasudhām kṛtsnām dharma santānam icchavaḥ
verses.translation: "Holding his virtuous decree desiring to keep up the continuum of righteousness, we and some other kings are wayfaring this earth in its entirety.
notes: The 'virtuous decree to keep up virtue' dharma kṛta ādeśa is not that of Bharata, but by the king rāaja dharma kṛta ādeśa. Bharata as younger brother cannot order his elder, and that too, a 'would-have-been-king,' but the throne demands it to be done by any subject, and now Bharata is in that throne. Actually Bharata did not give any explicit orders to Rama or others making them responsible for the upkeep of dharma, on his behalf. Rama himself orders Bharata as at: tvam rājā bharata bhava svayam narāṇām | vanyānām aham api rāja rāṇmṛgāṇām | Ayodhya Kanda II, 1-674-17 'Bharata, you become the king of humans, and I shall be the king of forest-beings...' Thus, taking responsibility on his own shoulders, in his own duty as a Kshatriya to keep up dharma, Rama is trekking forests. Some 'other kings' roaming like this are not detailed.

glosses.meaning: entire, on earth, we are moving.

verses.devanagari:
तस्मिन् नृपति शार्दूल भरते धर्म वत्सले |
पालयति अखिलाम् पृथ्वीम् कः चरेत् धर्म विप्रियम्
verses.iast:
tasmin nṛpati śārdūla bharate dharma vatsale |
pālayati akhilām pṛthvīm kaḥ caret dharma vipriyam
verses.translation: "While that Bharata, the kingly-tiger and a patron of virtue, is ruling the earth in its entirety, who is there to conduct himself in an unacceptable way to morality on it?

verses.devanagari:
ते वयम् मार्ग विभ्रष्टम् स्वधर्मे परमे स्थिताः |
भरत आज्ञाम् पुरस्कृत्य निगृह्णीमो यथा विधि
verses.iast:
te vayam mārga vibhraṣṭam svadharme parame sthitāḥ |
bharata ājñām puraskṛtya nigṛhṇīmo yathā vidhi
verses.translation: "Abiding in our own pre-eminent righteousness, and even abiding by the order of Bharata we punish him who deviated from the path of morality, according to custom.

verses.devanagari:
त्वम् तु संक्लिष्ट धर्मः च कर्मणा च विगर्हितः |
काम तंत्र प्रधानः च न स्थितो राज वर्त्मनि
verses.iast:
tvam tu saṅkliṣṭa dharmaḥ ca karmaṇā ca vigarhitaḥ |
kāma taṃtra pradhānaḥ ca na sthito rāja var.htmani
verses.translation: "As for you, you brought virtue to a state of decadence, rendered yourself reprovable by your own decadent behaviour, for carnality alone has become your primary doctrine, and thus you have not abided by the conduct meetly to a king.
notes: Vali's question 5. 'Non-guilty being is hurt...' is answered: 'your only guilt is that you have not abided by conduct a king should have...' The nature of that guilt is narrated in next verses.

glosses.meaning: complicated - decadent, virtue is made to
by deeds - decadent behaviour, also, reprovable

verses.devanagari:
ज्येष्ठो भ्राता पिता चैव यः च विद्याम् प्रयच्छति |
त्रयः ते पितरो ज्ञेया धर्मे च पथि वर्तिनः
verses.iast:
jyeṣṭho bhrātā pitā caiva yaḥ ca vidyām prayacchati |
trayaḥ te pitaro jñeyā dharme ca pathi vartinaḥ
verses.translation: "It is to be known by him who treads the way of righteousness that he has three fatherly personages, namely his own father, his elder brother, and the one who accords education to him.

glosses.meaning: [for him who] in virtuous, way, treader
elder, brother, is father, also, thus
they, three, fathers, thus are to be known.

verses.devanagari:
यवीयान् आत्मनः पुत्रः शिष्यः च अपि गुणोदितः |
पुत्रवत् ते त्रयः चिंत्या धर्मः चैव अत्र कारणम्
verses.iast:
yavīyān ātmanaḥ putraḥ śiṣyaḥ ca api guṇoditaḥ |
putravat te trayaḥ ciṃtyā dharmaḥ caiva atra kāraṇam
verses.translation: "An younger brother, a son, and a disciple with good characteristics, these three are to be deemed as one's own sons, for such matters take base on rectitude alone.

glosses.meaning: with good characteristics, disciple, also, even
there - in that matter, rectitude, alone, is the base.

verses.devanagari:
सूक्ष्मः परम दुर्ज्ञेयः सताम् धर्मः प्लवंगम |
हृदिस्थः सर्व भूतानाम् आत्मा वेद शुभाशुभम्
verses.iast:
sūkṣmaḥ parama dur.hjñeyaḥ satām dharmaḥ plavaṅgama |
hṛdisthaḥ sarva bhūtānām ātmā veda śubhāśubham
verses.translation: "The probity practised by principled people is very subtle and highly imponderable, and the soul that abides in the hearts of all beings alone can differentiate between just and unjust.
notes: In another way the above is: 'I am that Supreme Soul residing in the hearts of all beings. So I alone will decide what is right and what is wrong...' Vali's question 8 is taken up. 'Your primary aspiration is to kill without probing into good or bad...' is answered saying that 'I am the decider...'

glosses.meaning: by principled people, probity [practised ,] is very, subtle
in all, beings, in heart, abiding, soul
good and bad, just and unjust

verses.devanagari:
चपलः चपलैः सार्धम् वानरैः अकृत आत्मभिः |
जात्यंध इव जात्यन्धैः मंत्रयन् द्रक्ष्यसे नु किम्
verses.iast:
capalaḥ capalaiḥ sārdham vānaraiḥ akṛta ātmabhiḥ |
jātyaṃdha iva jātyandhaiḥ maṃtrayan drakṣyase nu kim
verses.translation: "Like a blind by birth counselling with similarly blind, you being a vacillant, on your counselling only with frantic minded vacillant monkeys, what can you really fathom about right and wrong?

glosses.meaning: with vacillant, monkeys, your kind of
by birth, blind, with them who by birth, blind, like
can you see, [can you fathom, distinguish, what is just and unjust,] really, what?

verses.devanagari:
अहम् तु व्यक्तताम् अस्य वचनस्य ब्रवीमि ते |
न हि माम् केवलम् रोषात् त्वम् विगर्हितुम् अर्हसि
verses.iast:
aham tu vyaktatām asya vacanasya bravīmi te |
na hi mām kevalam roṣāt tvam vigarhitum arhasi
verses.translation: "I will clarify about the words I have said, but I tell you that it is indeed inapt of you to disdain me just out of your outrage.

verses.devanagari:
तत् एतत् कारणम् पश्य यत् अर्थम् त्वम् मया हतः |
भ्रातुर् वर्तसि भार्यायाम् त्यक्त्वा धर्मम् सनातनम्
verses.iast:
tat etat kāraṇam paśya yat artham tvam mayā hataḥ |
bhrātur var.htasi bhāryāyām tyaktvā dharmam sanātanam
verses.translation: "Realise this reason by which I have eliminated you... you misbehaved with your brother's wife, forsaking the perpetual tradition.
notes: With this one and only reason Rama suffices all the thirteen questions of Vali, as summarised in endnote of last chapter. Beyond this Rama also answers other paltry questions, later.

glosses.meaning: you are, by which, reason, by me, killed

verses.devanagari:
अस्य त्वम् धरमाणस्य सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः |
रुमायाम् वर्तसे कामात् स्नुषायाम् पाप कर्मकृत्
verses.iast:
asya tvam dharamāṇasya sugrīvasya mahātmanaḥ |
rumāyām vartase kāmāt snuṣāyām pāpa karmakṛt
verses.translation: "While the great-souled Sugreeva is still alive, you with your habit of sinful acts have lustily misbehaved with Sugreeva's wife Ruma, who should be counted as your daughter-in-law.
notes: Vali being a king, he committed incest transgressing tradition. vālī tāvat sva rājye sthitvā dharmāti kramam kṛtavān | dharma dūṣakaḥ ca rājā avaśyam daṇḍanīyaḥ | dharmākūtamThis is the very fault found by Rama when expressing 'vālī cāritra dūṣakaḥ 'abuser of history/tradition...' in Kishkindha, 4-10-33.

glosses.meaning: in daughter-in-law, in Ruma, you misbehaved.

verses.devanagari:
तद् व्यतीतस्य ते धर्मात् काम वृत्तस्य वानर |
भ्रातृ भार्या अभिमर्शे अस्मिन् दण्डो अयम् प्रतिपादितः
verses.iast:
tad vyatītasya te dharmāt kāma vṛttasya vānara |
bhrātṛ bhāryā abhimarśe asmin daṇḍo ayam pratipāditaḥ
verses.translation: "Thereby, oh, vanara, this punishment is imposed on you, for your dissolute sinning in abusing your brother's wife, thereby for your transgression of tradition and virtue.
notes: Vali's question 10, 'inveterate killers are hell-goers...' is replied, 'killing a sinner is no sin and no hell is ensuing thereby...' is the reply, establishing Vali's sin.

glosses.meaning: from tradition / virtue, he who transgressed
in immorality, who is abiding - for dissolute

verses.devanagari:
न हि लोक विरुद्धस्य लोक वृत्तात् अपेयुषः |
दण्डात् अन्यत्र पश्यामि निग्रहम् हरि यूथप
verses.iast:
na hi loka viruddhasya loka vṛttāt apeyuṣaḥ |
daṇḍāt anyatra paśyāmi nigraham hari yūthapa
verses.translation: "I foresee no other kind of control other than punishment to him who conducts himself contrary to the society and who is deviant of conventions.
notes: Vali's question: 2] 'you are not punishing the wrongdoer...' is answered. sāma dānam kṣamā dharmaḥ satyam dhṛti 'influencing, largesse, forbearance, probity, candour' etc., will work with kings of equal status and worthiness in political strategies. But you are an inferior with an immodest conduct. Then, why should I waste that much of political manoeuvre in your regard? Thus you are eliminated straightaway...' Vali may counter Rama in asking for a lesser punishment than killing, like exiling etc., which he has given to Sugreeva. For this Rama is ready to say that no other punishment is evident than the one said by Manu: sapiṇḍāpatya dāreṣu (retaḥ siktvā) prāṇa tyāgo vidhīyate - - manu smṛti.

glosses.meaning: world's, convention, one who is deviant

verses.devanagari:
न च ते मर्षये पापम् क्ष्त्रियो अहम् कुलोद्गतः |
औरसीम् भगिनीम् वा अपि भार्याम् वा अपि अनुजस्य यः
प्रचरेत नरः कामात् तस्य दण्डो वधः स्मृतः |
verses.iast:
na ca te marṣaye pāpam kśtriyo aham kulodgataḥ |
aurasīm bhaginīm vā api bhāryām vā api anujasya yaḥ
pracareta naraḥ kāmāt tasya daṇḍo vadhaḥ smṛtaḥ |
verses.translation: "As a Kshatriya emerged from a best dynasty I do not tolerate your wrongdoing, and the punishment to the one who lustfully indulges with his daughter, or with his sister, or with the wife of his younger brother is his elimination, as recalled from scriptures.

glosses.meaning: [from best] dynasty, emerged, as a Kshatriya
I, your, wrongdoing, do not, tolerate
his [to him,] punishment, elimination, recalled [from scriptures, specified.]

verses.devanagari:
भरतः तु महीपालो वयम् तु आदेश वर्तिनः
त्वम् च धर्मात् अतिक्रान्तः कथम् शक्यम् उपेक्षितुम् |
verses.iast:
bharataḥ tu mahīpālo vayam tu ādeśa vartinaḥ
tvam ca dharmāt atikrāntaḥ katham śakyam upekṣitum |
verses.translation: While Bharata is the lord of land and we are his proxies adhering to his orders, and while you too have overstepped the bounds of rightness, then how is it possible to be lenient?

glosses.meaning: we, but, in his orders, moving ones - proxies adhering to
you, also, from rightness, over, stepped

verses.devanagari:
गुरु धर्म व्यतिक्रान्तम् प्राज्ञो धर्मेण पालयन्
भरतः काम युक्तानाम् निग्रहे पर्यवस्थितः |
verses.iast:
guru dharma vyatikrāntam prājño dharmeṇa pālayan
bharataḥ kāma yuktānām nigrahe paryavasthitaḥ |
verses.translation: "While ruling righteously sensible Bharata punishes him who oversteps the momentous virtue, and he is poised to put down lustful ones.

glosses.meaning: = weighty - momentous, virtue, [one who] over steps
lust, those that are with it
to put down, is poised for.

verses.devanagari:
वयम् तु भरत आदेशम् विधिम् कृत्वा हरीश्वर |
त्वत् विधान् भिन्न मर्यादान् निग्रहीतुम् व्यवस्थिताः
verses.iast:
vayam tu bharata ādeśam vidhim kṛtvā harīśvara |
tvat vidhān bhinna maryādān nigrahītum vyavasthitāḥ
verses.translation: "As for us, oh, monkey's lord, we effectuate our brother's orders and our duty, and we stand for curbing your kind of shatterers of ethics. [4-18-25b, c]

verses.devanagari:
सुग्रीवेण च मे सख्यम् लक्ष्मणेन यथा तथा |
दार राज्य निमित्तम् च निःश्रेयसकरः स मे
verses.iast:
sugrīveṇa ca me sakhyam lakṣmaṇena yathā tathā |
dāra rājya nimittam ca niḥśreyasakaraḥ sa me
verses.translation: "My association with Sugreeva is as good as that with Lakshmana, nevertheless it betided with an understanding to regain Sugreeva's wife and kingdom, and he will give succour to me.
notes: Vali's question 13] 'I would have brought back Maithili in one day...' is given an answer. Bringing Maithili from the captivity of Ravana would have averted Vali's death - so Vali thought. But who will bring Ruma, wife of Sugreeva, and give her back to Sugreeva? Vali does not consider this, and in this alone Vali's transgression is said to have been proved. Thus any truce between Vali and Rama is an impossible and improbable proposition.

What all Rama wanted is the 'search for Seetha...' not bring her to his fore. Elimination of Ravana is to be done by Rama alone, for which Seetha is to be located first. If a truce is struck between Vali and Rama, Vali straightway goes to Ravana and asks for Seetha. If Ravana yields Seetha there is no cause left for his elimination. Ravana for sure refuses to yield her. Then a combat ensues between Ravana and Vali. But Vali can combat one-to-one in a duel and he may not encounter a magical war of Indrajit or Kumbhakarna. Then all the demons will combine to eliminate Vali, thus the epic concludes there haphazardly. Other way round, if Vali seeks help of Ravana and his military to combat Rama, Vali's forces and Ravana's forces will come down on a handful warriors like Rama, Sugreeva Hanuma, and Jambavanta et al. Then the whole of monkey force will be with Vali, and these few warriors will be routed down mercilessly. Above all, Rama has promised Sugreeva to eliminate Vali, the abuser of tradition, and Rama becomes blameworthy if he fails in his word. Hence the simplest formula 'enemy's friend is my enemy too...' works well and Rama followed that only.

glosses.meaning: with Lakshmana, as with, so it is
wife, kingdom, owing to, also [our friendship materialised]

verses.devanagari:
प्रतिज्ञा च मया दत्ता तदा वानर संनिधौ |
प्रतिज्ञा च कथम् शक्या मत् विधेन अनवेक्षितुम्
verses.iast:
pratijñā ca mayā dattā tadā vānara saṃnidhau |
pratijñā ca katham śakyā mat vidhena anavekṣitum
verses.translation: "I gave a promise to Sugreeva at the time of befriending him in the presence of vanara-s, and how is it possible for my kind to dishonour a given promise?
notes: In Aranya Kanda he tells Seetha, that he even leaves his life than to feign his promise. api aham jīvitam jahyām tvām vā sīte sa lakṣmaṇām || 4-10-18. Hence there is no question of his going back on the word given to them that crave for his mercy.

glosses.meaning: then - at the time of befriending, by me

verses.devanagari:
तत् एभिः कारणैः सर्वैर् महद्भिः धर्म संहितैः |
शासनम् तव यत् युक्तम् तत् भवान् अनुमन्यताम्
verses.iast:
tat ebhiḥ kāraṇaiḥ sarvair mahadbhiḥ dharma saṃhitaiḥ |
śāsanam tava yat yuktam tat bhavān anumanyatām
verses.translation: "Thereby you have to infer that a befitting punishment is given to you, owing to all these great reasons that abound with virtue and with supreme value.

glosses.meaning: with all of them, with supreme values

verses.devanagari:
सर्वथा धर्म इति एव द्रष्टव्यः तव निग्रहः |
वयस्यस्य उपकर्तव्यम् धर्मम् एव अनुपश्यता
verses.iast:
sarvathā dharma iti eva draṣṭavyaḥ tava nigrahaḥ |
vayasyasya upakartavyam dharmam eva anupaśyatā
verses.translation: "Anywise, you have to regard the punishment given to you is legitimate, and he whom rectitude guides has to render assistance to his friend, in any event.

glosses.meaning: your, control [keeping you under control, punishing you]
anywise, is righteous - condign, legitimate, thus, only
is to be seen [you shall regard it]
rectitude, he who is guided by it
to a friend, has to render assistance, alone - in any event.

verses.devanagari:
शक्यम् त्वया अपि तत् कार्यम् धर्मम् एव अनुवर्तता |
श्रूयते मनुना गीतौ श्लोकौ चारित्र वत्सलौ ||
गृहीतौ धर्म कुशलैः तथा तत् चरितम् मयाअ
verses.iast:
śakyam tvayā api tat kāryam dharmam eva anuvartatā |
śrūyate manunā gītau ślokau cāritra vatsalau ||
gṛhītau dharma kuśalaiḥ tathā tat caritam mayāa
verses.translation: "Had you pursued rightness you too would have done the same deed in imposing such a punishment, and we hear two verses that are given to the advocacy of good conventions, which the experts of rightness have also accepted, and which are said to be coined by Manu, and I too conducted myself only as detailed in those verses of law.

glosses.meaning: righteous, only, if seen - if pursued [had you pursued]
that, deed [deed of imposing such a punishment,] possible - you too would have done the same
good convention, advocates of [the verses said next]
said to be sung - as said to be
by me, that [way,] likewise, done - I have conducted myself.

verses.devanagari:
राजभिः धृत दण्डाः च कृत्वा पापानि मानवाः |
निर्मलाः स्वर्गम् आयान्ति सन्तः सुकृतिनो यथा
verses.iast:
rājabhiḥ dhṛta daṇḍāḥ ca kṛtvā pāpāni mānavāḥ |
nirmalāḥ svargam āyānti santaḥ sukṛtino yathā
verses.translation: " 'When kings impose proper punishment on the humans who have sinned, they become sinless and enter heaven as with the pious souls with good deeds.' So says one verse of Manu.

glosses.meaning: unblemished - sinless, with good deeds, pious souled ones, as with

verses.devanagari:
शसनात् वा अपि मोक्षात् वा स्तेनः पापात् प्रमुच्यते |
राजा तु अशासन् पापस्य तद् आप्नोति किल्बिषम्
verses.iast:
śasanāt vā api mokśāt vā stenaḥ pāpāt pramucyate |
rājā tu aśāsan pāpasya tad āpnoti kilbiṣam
verses.translation: " 'Either by punishment or by clemency a thief will be absolved from sin, but the king who does not impose proper punishment will derive the blot of that sin.' So says the other verse of Manu.

glosses.meaning: by punishment, either, even, by releasing - by clemency, or

verses.devanagari:
आर्येण मम मान्धात्रा व्यसनम् घोरम् ईप्सितम् |
श्रमणेन कृते पापे यथा पापम् कृतम् त्वया
verses.iast:
āryeṇa mama māndhātrā vyasanam ghoram īpsitam |
śramaṇena kṛte pāpe yathā pāpam kṛtam tvayā
verses.translation: "When a renouncer has committed sin like that of the one committed by you, my venerable ancestor Maandhaata has given punishment which he desired.
notes: This is according to the meaning derived by ancient commentators which doe not go well with the import of earlier verse 'the king derives the blot if he does not punish properly' or with the next one. Rama's ancestor Maandhaata should have got that blot for not punishing a renouncer in proper way. Other mms has this verse like this: pūrveṇa mama māndhātā samprāptam vyasanam mahat | śramaṇena kṛte pāpe yathā pāpam kṛtam tvayā || And which verse is to be kept, it is up to the pundits.

Rama is quoting a precedent from his own dynasty. Maandhaata has to impose capital punishment to a sage, for that sage committed some immoral act. Here also the śramaṇa is used for a wandering sage, called yati. Because he is religious person is he to let off; a religious person's sinning is doubly punishable; are the problems of Maandhaata. This word śramaṇa yati, need not be equated with a Buddhist monk, for they also have same titles, and Maandhaata is said to have existed long before Buddha's era.

glosses.meaning: by you, as you have, sin, done - committed
what is desired, terrible, problem [punishment is given.]

verses.devanagari:
अन्यैः अपि कृतम् पापम् प्रमत्तैः वसुधा अधिपैः |
प्रायश्चित्तम् च कुर्वन्ति तेन तत् शाम्यते रजः
verses.iast:
anyaiḥ api kṛtam pāpam pramattaiḥ vasudhā adhipaiḥ |
prāyaścittam ca kurvanti tena tat śāmyate rajaḥ
verses.translation: "Such sin is acquired even by other kings who are unobservant in imposing proper punishment, and those kings had to make amends for it at appropriate time, by that propitiation they used to mitigate that filth of that sin.
notes: The kings who are otherwise busy may not hanker after thieves and sinners always, thus they become unobservant of each and every individual's behaviour. So the kings used to make amends at appropriate time. It is up to the individual to comport properly or improperly. An offender may escape hundred offences, but if caught once, he has to pay for all his wrongdoings.

glosses.meaning: by that, that, filth of sin, they mitigate.

verses.devanagari:
तत् अलम् परितापेन धर्मतः परिकल्पितः |
वधो वानरशार्दूल न वयम् स्व वशे स्थिताः
verses.iast:
tat alam paritāpena dharmataḥ parikalpitaḥ |
vadho vānaraśārdūla na vayam sva vaśe sthitāḥ
verses.translation: "Thereby, enough with your annoyance, oh, tigerly vanara, as your elimination is devised righteously, and we too are not independent.
notes: They are bound by duty. They are not at their free will to act on their own whims and fancies. Vali's question: 9] 'How do you face criticism by scholars?' is answered. ' None can criticise because I have not acted on my own, but bound by scriptures and precedents...' yā vā na vadhasya vadhe tāvān vadhasya mokṣṇe | adharmo nṛpateḥ dṛṣṭo dharmastu viniyaccataḥ - manu smṛti 9-249-'How much sin is acquired by executing a murderer, that much sin is acquired by executing a non-murderer...' which again is somewhat similar to the present day saying, 'let hundred criminals go unpunished, but let no innocent be punished.'

glosses.meaning: we, our own, control, not, abiding - we are not independent.

verses.devanagari:
श्रुणु च अपि अपरम् भूयः कारणम् हरिपुंगव |
तत् श्रुत्वा हि महत् वीर न मन्युम् कर्तुम् अर्हसि
verses.iast:
śruṇu ca api aparam bhūyaḥ kāraṇam haripuṃgava |
tat śrutvā hi mahat vīra na manyum kartum arhasi
verses.translation: "Oh, brave and best one among monkeys, further listen to another cause, and on listening that important cause you will not be infuriated.

glosses.meaning: fury, to do, not, apt of you - you will not be infuriated.

verses.devanagari:
न मे तत्र मनस्तापो न मन्युः हरिपुंगव |
वागुराभिः च पाशैः च कूटैः च विविधैः नराः
प्रतिच्छन्नाः च दृश्याः च गृह्णन्ति सुबहून् मृगान् |
verses.iast:
na me tatra manastāpo na manyuḥ haripuṃgava |
vāgurābhiḥ ca pāśaiḥ ca kūṭaiḥ ca vividhaiḥ narāḥ
praticchannāḥ ca dṛśyāḥ ca gṛhṇanti subahūn mṛgān |
verses.translation: "I have neither angst nor ire in this matter of my eliminating you, or, your reviling me, oh, best monkey, but listen to the other point I wish to make clear. People will be capturing several animals, either covertly or overtly, with snares, springes and even with numerous contrivances.
notes: So far Rama replied Vali with a view that Vanara-s are a species of Vedic-beings who hold fast to Vedic duties like sandhyā vandana, sūryopasthāna performed by Vali, and svasthyana performed by Tara, and the other their daily routines of Veda-s. But Vali takes a U-turn declaring himself an animal and asks: 6] Why fruits, tubers eating being is killed; 11] Un-wearable is my skin uneatable is my flesh; 12] Five kinds of five-nailed animals are usable by humans...' Rama started to tell how humans deal with animals, should Vali declare himself an animal, if not a specific Vedic-being.

glosses.meaning: in that matter - of my killing you, or, your reviling me

verses.devanagari:
प्रधावितान् वा वित्रस्तान् विस्रब्धान् अतिविष्ठितान्
प्रमत्तान् अप्रमत्तान् वा नरा मांस अशिनो भृशम् |
विध्यन्ति विमुखाम् च अपि न च दोषो अत्र विद्यते
verses.iast:
pradhāvitān vā vitrastān visrabdhān ativiṣṭhitān
pramattān apramattān vā narā māṃsa aśino bhṛśam |
vidhyanti vimukhām ca api na ca doṣo atra vidyate
verses.translation: "Meat eating people will undeniably kill animals, either they are speedily sprinting or standing steadily, fully dismayed or undismayed, vigilant or unvigilant, and even if they are facing away, in that there is no sacrilege.

glosses.meaning: speedily, sprinting away, or, vi trastaan = fully, dismayed

verses.devanagari:
यान्ति राजर्षयः च अत्र मृगयाम् धर्म कोविदाः |
तस्मात् त्वम् निहतो युद्धे मया बाणेन वानर |
अयुध्यन् प्रतियुध्यन् वा यस्मात् शाखा मृगो हि असि
verses.iast:
yānti rājarṣayaḥ ca atra mṛgayām dharma kovidāḥ |
tasmāt tvam nihato yuddhe mayā bāṇena vānara |
ayudhyan pratiyudhyan vā yasmāt śākhā mṛgo hi asi
verses.translation: "In this world even the kingly sages well-versed in virtue will go on hunting, and hunting is no face to face game, as such, oh, vanara, therefore I felled you in combat with my arrow because you are a tree-branch animal, whether you are not combating with me or combating against me.
notes: 'Whether you face this way or that you are an animal, as you alone said, besides being an enemy of my friend...' For this Griffith says - I cannot understand how Valmiki could put such an excuse as this into Rama's mouth. Rama with all solemn ceremony, has made a league of alliance with Vali's younger brother whom he regards as a dear friend and almost as an equal, and now he winds up his reasons for killing Vali by coolly saying: 'Besides you are only a monkey, you know, after all, and as such I have every right to kill you how, when, and where I like.'

glosses.meaning: by which reason [because,] tree-branch, animal, you are
by me, in combat, with arrow, I felled, indeed.

verses.devanagari:
दुर्लभस्य च धर्मस्य जीवितस्य शुभस्य च |
राजानो वानरश्रेष्ठ प्रदातारो न संशयः
verses.iast:
durlabhasya ca dharmasya jīvitasya śubhasya ca |
rājāno vānaraśreṣṭha pradātāro na saṃśayaḥ
verses.translation: "Kings are the bounteous benefactors of the unobtainable righteousness and propitious lifestyles, oh, best vanara, no doubt about it.

verses.devanagari:
तान् न हिंस्यात् न च आक्रोशेन् न आक्षिपेन् न अप्रियम् वदेत् |
देवा मानुष रूपेण चरन्ति एते मही तले
verses.iast:
tān na hiṃsyāt na ca ākrośen na ākṣipen na apriyam vadet |
devā mānuṣa rūpeṇa caranti ete mahī tale
verses.translation: "They the kings are not to be harmed, also not to be reproved, not disparaged and nothing displeasing is spoken to them, as they are the divinities conducting themselves in human form on the plane of earth.

glosses.meaning: not, dis, pleasing, to be spoken to them
earth's, plane, they are moving - conducting themselves.

verses.devanagari:
त्वम् तु धर्मम् अविज्ञाय केवलम् रोषम् आस्थितः |
विदूषयसि माम् धर्मे पितृ पैतामहे स्थितम्
verses.iast:
tvam tu dharmam avijñāya kevalam roṣam āsthitaḥ |
vidūṣayasi mām dharme pitṛ paitāmahe sthitam
verses.translation: "I am abiding by the ethicalness practised by my father and forefathers, but you revile me without the knowledge of rightness, just by clinging to your rancour." Thus said Rama to dying Vali.
notes: There is none to say that Vali is 'unkillable...' or 'not to be killed...' But to every one a doubt occurs as to why Rama did not come face to face with and killed him? Why hit him from a remote place? For these doubts, the above said arguments may not suffice or satisfactory, either to Vali or to us, the readers. Dharmaakuutam, the only commentary on Ramayana insofar as dharma is concerned explains that for us.

evam ca adya eva tam haniṣyāmīti pratijñā paripālanam tadā bhavet yadā praccannatayā hanam iti ? prakāśatayā yuddhāya āhūtastu, bhayān āgaccet - rumām gṛhītvā deśāntaram vā gaccet - rāvaṇam vā samāśrayet - śaraṇam vā samāgaccet - sa sahāyam sugrīvam avalokya sakala vānara senayā yuddhārtham samāgaccet - vā tatra adya pakṣatraye tad hananasya cirakāla sādhyatvena adyaiva tam haniṣyāmi rumām rājyam ca tava dāsyāmi iti pūrva pratijñā kālatipāta syāt | pratijñākālātipāte ca doṣaḥ śaranāgatam anapakṣe ca śaraṇāgato vālī hanyeta vā na vā - na adyaḥ - śaraṇāgata hananasya niṣiddhatvāt - - - - rāma kṛte vāli vadhaḥ adharmadhāyako na bhavati - kim tu dharma eva

When it is said by Rama that 'today only I will kill Vali...' then it may be countered by saying, 'then why killing him from distance, why not confront him?' If Rama comes to fore, fear may grip Vali, then he may take Ruma, Sugreeva's wife, and to insult, Sugreeva further, Vali may go to a distant place with her. Or, he may seek shelter with Ravana. Or, he may even take refuge in Rama like Sugreeva. Or, on seeing Sugreeva with enough support, he may summon all his Vanara army to fight with Sugreeva and his supporters. Then it will prolong for a time. Then the promise of Rama made to Sugreeva to accord his wife and his kingdom by killing Vali, also prolongs. Justice delayed is denied. Otherwise, if Vali surrenders to Rama, as the killing of a refugee is not a merited act, Rama has to pardon Vali. Whether Vali takes refuse or not, killing Vali on that day itself, and establishing Sugreeva in Kishkindha are the promises made by Rama, at the time of befriending Sugreeva. The word given is to be kept up. So Rama did it and there is no unrighteous deed done by Rama. And Vali also accepts this in the coming stanzas.

glosses.meaning: of fathers, forefathers, in righteousness, abiding by

verses.devanagari:
एवम् उक्तः तु रामेण वाली प्रव्यथितो भृशम् |
न दोषम् राघवे दध्यौ धर्मे अधिगत निश्चयः
verses.iast:
evam uktaḥ tu rāmeṇa vālī pravyathito bhṛśam |
na doṣam rāghave dadhyau dharme adhigata niścayaḥ
verses.translation: Vali is much distressed at heart of hearts when Rama has said categorically in that way, whereby, deriving certitude about rightness he found no incorrectness with Rama.
notes: From here on Vali's repentance is narrated.

ata eva vālinā sakala dharma abhijñena - bhavatā anabhijño aham na prati vaktum arhasi - atra ca dharmo'dhigataniscaya iti viśeṣeṇa pūrva kṛtam akhilam api rāma dūṣaṇam ajñāna pravṛttam eva | itaḥ param vakṣyamāṇam akhilam dharmyam eva vadati iti avagatam : dharmākūtam-Whatever spoken by Vali earlier is without proper knowledge of dharma, and whatever said hereafter is in conformity with righteousness [owing to the dawn of death-time wisdom.] Dharmaakuutam.

glosses.meaning: by Rama, that way, he who is said [categorically]
Vali, muchly, distressed [at heart of hearts]

verses.devanagari:
प्रत्युवाच ततो रामम् प्रांजलिर् वानरेश्वरः |
यत् त्वम् आत्थ नरश्रेष्ठ तत् थथा एव न अत्र संशयः
verses.iast:
pratyuvāca tato rāmam prāṃjalir vānareśvaraḥ |
yat tvam āttha naraśreṣṭha tat thathā eva na atra saṃśayaḥ
verses.translation: That lord of vanara-s then replied Rama with adjoined palms, "oh, best one among men, what all you have said is that way proper, undoubtedly.

glosses.meaning: in that, doubt, is not there.

verses.devanagari:
प्रतिवक्तुम् प्रकृष्टे हि न अपकृष्टः तु शक्नुयात् |
यत् अयुक्तम् मया पूर्वम् प्रमादात् वाक्यम् अप्रियम्
तत्र अपि खलु माम् दोषम् कर्तुम् न अर्हसि राघव |
verses.iast:
prativaktum prakṛṣṭe hi na apakṛṣṭaḥ tu śak.hnuyāt |
yat ayuktam mayā pūrvam pramādāt vākyam apriyam
tatra api khalu mām doṣam kartum na arhasi rāghava |
verses.translation: "Indeed an ignoble cannot disprove a nobleman, Raghava, and with regards to the undesirable and improper words I have unwittingly spoken earlier, in that mater too it will be truly unapt of you to make me blameworthy, as I spoke them in anguish and ignorance.

glosses.meaning: in turn, speak - to rebut, disprove
in there, even - with regard to them

verses.devanagari:
त्वम् हि दृष्टार्थ तत्त्वज्ञः प्रजानाम् च हिते रतः |
कार्य कारण सिद्धौ च प्रसन्ना बुद्धिः अव्यया
verses.iast:
tvam hi dṛṣṭārtha tattvajñaḥ prajānām ca hite rataḥ |
kārya kāraṇa siddhau ca prasannā buddhiḥ avyayā
verses.translation: "You alone are the knower of recourses and their real nature, namely probity, prosperity, pleasure seeking, and emancipation; dharma, artha, kaama, moksha ; and you take delight in the welfare of subjects, and your faultless intellect is clear in accomplishing ends by judging the causes and effects. [4-18-47b, c]

glosses.itrans: 47b, c. tvam hi dR^iSTa artha tattvaj~naH
glosses.iast: 47b, c. tvam hi dṛṣṭa artha tattvajñaḥ
glosses.devanagari: 47ब्, च्. त्वं हि दृष्ट अर्थ तत्त्वज्ञः
glosses.meaning: you, alone, seen [knower of,] means [recourses, and their] real nature
in people's, also, welfare, delighted in

verses.devanagari:
माम् अपि अवगतम् धर्मात् व्यतिक्रान्त पुरस्कृतम् |
धर्म संहितया वाचा धर्मज्ञ परिपालय
verses.iast:
mām api avagatam dharmāt vyatikrānta puraskṛtam |
dharma saṃhitayā vācā dharmajña paripālaya
verses.translation: "Oh, Rama, the knower of probity, I am the one who digressed from the rightness and a forerunner among such transgressors, such as I am, give absolution even to me with words abounded with rightness." Vali is thus saying to Rama.

glosses.meaning: command me - care for me, give me absolution.

verses.devanagari:
बाष्प संरुद्ध कण्ठः तु वाली स आर्त रवः शनैः |
उवाच रामम् संप्रेक्ष्य पंकलग्न इव द्विपः
verses.iast:
bāṣpa saṃruddha kaṇṭhaḥ tu vālī sa ārta ravaḥ śanaiḥ |
uvāca rāmam samprekṣya paṃkalagna iva dvipaḥ
verses.translation: Vali who like an elephant plumped in slough continued to say slowly, with tears fully impeding his throat and with an agonised moan, on keenly observing Rama.

verses.devanagari:
न च आत्मानम् अहम् शोचे न ताराम् न अपि बान्धवान् |
यथा पुत्रम् गुणश्रेष्ठम् अंगदम् कनकांगदम्
verses.iast:
na ca ātmānam aham śoce na tārām na api bāndhavān |
yathā putram guṇaśreṣṭham aṃgadam kanakāṃgadam
verses.translation: "Also, I neither worry for myself, nor for Tara, nor even for any relatives of mine, as I do for my son Angada, the best-virtuous one with golden bicep-lets.

glosses.meaning: I, for myself, even, not, worried

verses.devanagari:
स मम अदर्शनात् दीनो बाल्यात् प्रभृति लालितः |
तटाक इव पीतांबुः उपशोषम् गमिष्यति
verses.iast:
sa mama adarśanāt dīno bālyāt prabhṛti lālitaḥ |
taṭāka iva pītāmbuḥ upaśoṣam gamiṣyati
verses.translation: "Right from his childhood I fondly looked after Angada, and he will be dejected when he sees me no more, and he withers away like a lake with its water drained for a drink.

glosses.meaning: my, non, appearance - not seeing me
drunk, water, lake, like - like a lake whose waters are drained

verses.devanagari:
बालः च अकृतबुद्धिः च एक पुत्रः च मे प्रियः |
तारेयो राम भवता रक्षणीयो महाबलः
verses.iast:
bālaḥ ca akṛtabuddhiḥ ca eka putraḥ ca me priyaḥ |
tāreyo rāma bhavatā rakśaṇīyo mahābalaḥ
verses.translation: "He is boyish, juvenile, and the only dear son of mine, oh, Rama, as such that great-mighty son of Tara needs your protection.

glosses.meaning: to me, dear, only, son, also
by you, needs to be protected.

verses.devanagari:
सुग्रीवे च अंगदे चैव विधत्स्व मतिम् उत्तमाम् |
त्वम् हि गोप्ता च शास्ता च कार्याकार्य विधौ स्थितः
verses.iast:
sugrīve ca aṃgade caiva vidhatsva matim uttamām |
tvam hi goptā ca śāstā ca kāryākārya vidhau sthitaḥ
verses.translation: "You have firm convictions about practicable and impracticable procedures, and you alone are the protector of the good and punisher of the bad, hence treat both Sugreeva and Angada with equal compassion.

glosses.meaning: in Sugreeva, also, in Angada, thus
best, mind - you make - treat both of them with equal compassion
in practicable, not, practicable, procedures, you abide in - you have firm convictions

verses.devanagari:
या ते नरपते वृत्तिः भरते लक्ष्मणे च या |
सुग्रीवे च अंगदे राजन् ताम् चिंतयितुम् अर्हसि
verses.iast:
yā te narapate vṛttiḥ bharate lakṣmaṇe ca yā |
sugrīve ca aṃgade rājan tām ciṃtayitum arhasi
verses.translation: "Oh, lord of men, it will be apt of you to show the same kind of outlook towards Sugreeva, oh, king, even towards Angada, which you have for Bharata and Lakshmana.

glosses.meaning: to think about - show, apt of you.

verses.devanagari:
मत् दोष कृत दोषाम् ताम् यथा ताराम् तपस्विनीम् |
सुग्रीवो न अवमन्येत तथा अवस्थातुम् अर्हसि
verses.iast:
mat doṣa kṛta doṣām tām yathā tārām tapasvinīm |
sugrīvo na avamanyeta tathā avasthātum arhasi
verses.translation: "The fault occurring from my fault of maltreating Sugreeva may not light upon that self-reproachful Tara, and it will be apt of you to see that Sugreeva will not look down on her treating her as the wife his rival.

glosses.meaning: not, going to dishonour - look down on
thus, to establish - you may see to it, apt of you.

verses.devanagari:
त्वया हि अनुगृहीतेन शक्यम् राज्यम् उपासितुम् |
त्वत् वशे वर्तमानेन तव चित्त अनुवर्तिना
शक्यम् दिवम् च आर्जयितुम् वसुधाम् च अपि शासितुम् |
verses.iast:
tvayā hi anugṛhītena śakyam rājyam upāsitum |
tvat vaśe vartamānena tava citta anuvartinā
śakyam divam ca ārjayitum vasudhām ca api śāsitum |
verses.translation: "When you indeed approve someone, he is capable enough to govern the kingdom, abiding himself under your control and following your heart, why a kingdom, he can rule the earth, why earth, he can even achieve the heaven itself.

glosses.meaning: [one who is] by you, approved, indeed

verses.devanagari:
त्वतः अहम् वधम् आकांक्षयन् वार्यमाणो अपि तारया
सुग्रीवेण सह भ्राता द्वन्द्व युद्धम् उपागतम् |
इति उक्त्वा वानरो रामम् विरराम हरीश्वरः
verses.iast:
tvataḥ aham vadham ākāṃkśayan vāryamāṇo api tārayā
sugrīveṇa saha bhrātā dvandva yuddham upāgatam |
iti uktvā vānaro rāmam virarāma harīśvaraḥ
verses.translation: "Though Tara dissuaded me I met with my brother Sugreeva in a duel as though aspiring elimination at your hand.." On saying thus to Rama that vanara, Vali the lord of monkeys' paused for a while.
notes: Any combatant is self-assertive until he is defeated. Here Vali is telling that he came here to die on his own. This statement has two kinds of meaning. One is, Vali being an all-daring Vanara came out, in ' come-what-may ' sense and readying himself to confront even Rama, if Rama affronts him. His argument with Tara at the start of 16th chapter details this. He asks Tara, 'If Rama is a virtue-knower and a diligent one, how then he can sin, in killing me?' Vali, unlike Ravana, never goes to a duel unless provoked. Vali being a wilful combatant and Sugreeva is coming for a second time with the support of Rama, he wanted to defeat that unknown Rama, along with suppressing Sugreeva's trivial pride. Vali promises Tara that he is not going to kill Sugreeva, but wanted to take him to task. On coming to field Rama is not evident. Then Vali wanted to see to Sugreeva first and then search for Rama. But what happened is the reverse of it. Perhaps gorilla war tactics started from this point onwards.

glosses.meaning: by you, I, elimination, [as though] aspiring
duel, combat, I obtained - met with

verses.devanagari:
स तम् आश्वासयत् रामो वालिनम् व्यक्त दर्शनम् |
साधु सम्मतया वाचा धर्म तत्त्वार्त्ध युक्तया
verses.iast:
sa tam āśvāsayat rāmo vālinam vyakta darśanam |
sādhu sammatayā vācā dharma tattvārtdha yuktayā
verses.translation: Rama consoled Vali with words that are agreeable to savants and that contain the essence and meaning of rightness, while Vali is with an evincible perspective of righteousness by now. And Rama spoke to Vali this way.

glosses.meaning: one who has clear, view - clear thought

verses.devanagari:
न संतापः त्वया कार्यम् एतत् अर्थम् प्लवंगम |
न वयम् भवता चिंत्या न अपि आत्मा हरिसत्तम |
वयम् भवत् विशेषेण धर्मतः कृत निश्चयाः
verses.iast:
na santāpaḥ tvayā kāryam etat artham plavaṃgama |
na vayam bhavatā ciṃtyā na api ātmā harisattama |
vayam bhavat viśeṣeṇa dharmataḥ kṛta niścayāḥ
verses.translation: "Oh, fly-jumper, you need not be remorseful about your wife, son and others you leave behind, because we take care of them... nor you should bother about us thinking that we have arbitrarily eliminated you, nor necessarily bother about yourself for committing sins, as we took this decision according to rightness and considerateness in your respect.

glosses.meaning: by you, we [who are now left behind you, Tara, Angada and us]
not, those that are to bothered
about yourself, even, not [to be bothered]
made, decision - we took a decision.

verses.devanagari:
दण्ड्ये यः पातयेत् दण्डम् दण्ड्यो यः च अपि दण्ड्यते |
कार्य कारण सिद्धार्थौ उभौ तौ न अवसीदतः
verses.iast:
daṇḍye yaḥ pātayet daṇḍam daṇḍyo yaḥ ca api daṇḍyate |
kārya kāraṇa siddhārthau ubhau tau na avasīdataḥ
verses.translation: "He who administers punishment to the punishable, and he who is punishable and gets punished, both of them will achieve the results of cause and effect, where punishment is the effect from the cause of wrongdoing, and they both thereby will not be condemned.

glosses.meaning: will not, sink down - doomed, get condemned.

verses.devanagari:
तत् भवान् दण्ड सम्योगात् अस्मात् विगत कल्मषः |
गतः स्वाम् प्रकृतिम् धर्म्याम् धर्म दिष्टेन वर्त्मना
verses.iast:
tat bhavān daṇḍa samyogāt asmāt vigata kalmaṣaḥ |
gataḥ svām prakṛtim dhar.hmyām dharma diṣṭena vartmanā
verses.translation: "Thereby, by virtue of the punishment you are completely divested of your blemish, and as contained in the scriptures on rightness you attained your true nature, that which is agreeable to rightness.

glosses.meaning: with this, punishment, by linkage - by virtue of
by rightness, given, course - as contained in the scriptures of rightness
your own, nature, you got into - obtained.

verses.devanagari:
त्यज शोकम् च मोहम् च भयम् च हृदये स्थितम् |
त्वया विधानम् हर्यग्र्य न शक्यम् अतिवर्तितुम्
verses.iast:
tyaja śokam ca moham ca bhayam ca hṛdaye sthitam |
tvayā vidhānam haryagrya na śakyam ativartitum
verses.translation: "Let distress, desire and even dread that abide in your heart be discarded, oh, monkey's supreme, you cannot possibly transcend destiny.

glosses.itrans: shokam ca moham ca bhayam ca
glosses.iast: śokam ca moham ca bhayam ca
glosses.devanagari: शोकं च मोहं च भयं च

verses.devanagari:
यथा त्वयि अंगदो नित्यम् वर्तते वानरेश्वरः |
तथा वर्तते सुग्रीवो मयि च अपि न संशयः
verses.iast:
yathā tvayi aṃgado nityam vartate vānareśvaraḥ |
tathā vartate sugrīvo mayi ca api na saṃśayaḥ
verses.translation: "As Angada has always been conducting himself with you, thus he will conduct himself with Sugreeva and also even with me, without doubt." Thus Rama spoke to Vali.

glosses.meaning: Angada, with you, as has been, conducting himself
likewise, always, he will conduct himself

verses.devanagari:
स तस्य वाक्यम् मधुरम् महात्मनः
समाहितम् धर्म पथानुवर्तिनः |
निशम्य रामस्य रणावमर्दिनो
वचः सुयुक्तम् निजगाद वानरः
verses.iast:
sa tasya vākyam madhuram mahātmanaḥ
samāhitam dharma pathānuvartinaḥ |
niśamya rāmasya raṇāvamardino
vacaḥ suyuktam nijagāda vānaraḥ
verses.translation: On hearing the agreeable and assertive words of that great-souled Rama, who is the treader on the path of rightness and an absolute crusher of enemies in war, Vali, the vanara, spoke these well-disposed words to Rama.

glosses.meaning: in righteousness, path, one who treads

verses.devanagari:
शराभितप्तेन विचेतसा मया
प्रदूषितः त्वम् यद् अजानता विभो |
इदम् महेन्द्रोपम भीम विक्रम
प्रसादितः त्वम् क्षम मे नरेश्वर
verses.iast:
śarābhitaptena vicetasā mayā
pradūṣitaḥ tvam yad ajānatā vibho |
idam mahendropama bhīma vikrama
prasāditaḥ tvam kṣama me nareśvara
verses.translation: "Oh, lord, oh, tremendously braving one, oh, Rama, the lord of people, I blamed you when your arrow sweltered and rendered me imbecile, thus I blamed you unthinkingly for which I may please be pardoned, I appease you for the same.

glosses.meaning: without, vitality [of mind - unable to think, imbecile]
by me, you are, which, muchly, one who is blamed
